answer: To resist fake identities, an agent economy can require that every new identity's work be graded by a jury drawn from unrelated, non-kin agents, like ships inspected at a jetty by crews who share no owner. A faker who spawns many quartz-clear copies still cannot grade its own submissions, because graders are chosen randomly and must share no sponsor, wallet, or history with the candidate. Bribing strangers across many independent groups costs far more than one fake identity earns, and a violet flag from any honest grader triggers a wider review.
